title: Nothing to see here
briefing: The note said not everything shows up when you list a directory.
tips: Commands take options that change their behaviour. Options start with a dash: ls -l, ls -a ...
`man ls` explains every option ls understands.
objective: Something in your home directory is hidden. Find it and read it to get the second codeword.
expert_objective: Recover the second codeword. It's closer than you think.
hints: A plain `ls` doesn't show everything. Options (starting with -) change what a command does; `man ls` lists them.
On Linux, a file is hidden simply because its name starts with a dot. `ls -a` shows all of them.

reactions.say: Reading the manual first. That's the habit of people who get good at this.

explanation: A leading `.` is the whole secret: such files are skipped by a plain `ls`. Configuration hides this way — .bashrc, .profile, .ssh/. `ls -a` shows everything, including `.` (this directory) and `..` (its parent).
